name: Tønsberg Brygge
description: Located in Tønsberg, Tønsberg Brygge is a local business offering local flavor. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town. Historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. It became an important trading center and was founded by Vikings in the 9th century. In fact, Tonsberg Old Cemetery contains 22 war graves, of the First World War, 14 of them unidentified by name, but all naval casualties from the Battle of Jutland in 1916. This town is charming with it's cobblestone streets, in particular near their shopping district. I used to live in this town back in 2017, for about half of the year. Visiting the brygge, (pier) was always such a nice and tranquil escape. Their are plenty of restaurants outlined near the brygge. Some of the restaurants were diverse within their culinary range and the food wasn't too bad. I did not have the best culinary experience in Norway, but they did have a decent Indian restaurant by the pier. Local caught seafood was fresh and of good quality. They typically displayed that sort of fare during the farmers market. The pier would be freezing towards the autumn and winter seasons. The townsfolk launch their old historical boats during the holiday season and it is a sight to see. Many of the cafes, coffee shops and restaurants would close by 8-9 pm. Grocery stores and many shoppes were closed on Sundays. As an American, it was a bit of a culture shock. But the major differences I experienced in this town drove me towards introspection and deep growth. The glassy icey water reminded of a mirror upon self reflection. I may have been on the outside looking in, but it was a beautiful ponderous ride. I recommend visiting the pier and just overall experiencing this quiet, elegant town.

reviewPage.theExperience: The atmosphere leaned relaxed and easygoing.

name: Daiso
description: Daiso serves Sugar Land as a local business, with discount store at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Clean, new, Daiso shoppe! I'm liking this new location in the burbs' even more than the original in the city. This location of Daiso is sparkling clean & super organized. They pretty much have every random item that you're looking for. Items that you might not even need, but eventually grow accustomed to! Daiso has quality products that are shipped from Japan, which is why I was surprised that this location was stocked up to the brim. Although much smaller than the location in the city; it's basically compacted and has the same products. This location is situated in the heart of Sugar Land, specifically within the mini Asian plaza. The plaza has grown so much in the past few years and it's a warm welcome to have Daiso in the burbs'. A colorful spot full of random niknaks, food products and home furnishings. You'll basically find something for everyone in this little shoppe. It's a neat spot for practical gift giving ideas. I brought my toddler nephew here, and he was thrilled to find toy cars. They have awesome toys for the youngins' and cute kitchen items for the older folk. Most products are $5 & under. You'll be able to pinch pennies & save quite a lot. All in all, this fun little shoppe always comes through. It'll definitely be a spot to revisit again whenever in the S.L. area.

description: Buc-ee’s – Richmond is a local business in Richmond, with a focus on gas stations, convenience stores, car wash. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: This is just a simple and quick grab n go Buc-ees. If you're randomly craving for their in store snacks and treats, you'll find that here. They have the usual assortment of hot coffee, deli items and baked goods. I like their coffee! Strong, piping hot and far from bitter. I'm more of a pour over gal these days. No complaints. It's tastes just like their other locations. Granted, this location is much smaller than their other store fronts; but you'll find many of their products here. It has less bells and whistles though. If you're looking for souvenirs and actual gifts, you'll find it at their much larger locations. This one has an attached gas station and carwash just like the other ones. I've heard good things about their car wash so will definitely revisit. I was able to grab my favorite banana pudding and their coffee. Service was quick and simple. They've got plenty of cold bottled beverages and other random necessities such as milk, eggs, etc. This location isn't too far from Sugar Land so I frequent it every once in awhile. Parking is a bit tight but again, this it totally a grab and go location. Toodle-oo!

Parking is not as simple in this location but you can park near the houses. There are a few seasonal coffee flavors to choose from for the perk. Served with an ample amount of apple spice butter. I think they paired so nicely with the cappuccino. Overall, I was quite pleased with this experience. description: Dunkin' serves Westchase, Houston as a coffee and tea stop, with donuts, coffee & tea at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Dunkin donuts serves up some decent hot coffee, always crisp and tasty. Whether hot or cold, the coffee here is a good alternative from Starbucks. Grabbed an iced coffee today with just half amount of pumpkin spice flavoring. Paired it with a pumpkin spiced cake donut which wasn't bad. But it could have been fresh. It was oily to the touch. Maybe earlier in the morning it would taste different. I don't know. The donuts here are not that fresh which is my biggest gripe. We don't have that many locations of Dunkins here in the city, wish this location was better. The donuts have a bit of an smell to them, and taste a bit artificial. Other than that, this location has a drive thru which is convenient. Service has always been good. Can't complain. Recently I visited a Dunkins location in Alabama and tried their donuts. Flavor and freshness of the donuts were better. Hope they can improve within the state of Texas, otherwise may have to visit Shipley's for better quality products.

name: Taizzi Sushi – Katy
description: Taizzi Sushi – Katy serves Katy as a casual restaurant, with sushi bars, japanese, asian fusion at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Roll with the tides! Taizzi Sushi in Katy isn't too far from the local mall. Decided to stop by on a whim with a good friend for dinner. I thought the food here was pretty decent. They've got quite a large selection of grub to choose from the menu. I spotted Korean style ramen, bimbimbap, and even poke bowls on the menu. This spot is known for their AYCE selection or just wing it a la carte. Settled in for sushi because that's what this place is known for. First of all, the plaza is tiny and the restaurant is cramped as well. Surprisingly though on a Saturday night, we found decent parking and it wasn't too busy inside the restaurant. Most likely due to the holidays. Service was impeccable, I mean it's a small place so the servers continuously checked up on us. One of them even offered me a fork since I'm not the biggest fan of using chopsticks. Lol. I'd say my favorite item was the baked sushi. I've always been a fan of baked sushi and they've got a decent selection for that kinda grub. The baked salmon sushi that we ordered was tender and quite flavorful. I definitely want to try the baked lobster option next time. Runner up was the peppered tuna sashimi and pink lady sushi. Both of these items had a bite and kick to them. The jasmine tea that was served wasn't that good though; just flat and lukewarm. The interior inside here is dark and cozy, decent for a dinner vibe, in which we settled upon that evening. I don't eat this kinda grub that often but this spot was quite chill. Clean and minimal. They've got a tv inside blasting Korean music that is sure to keep you awake with all the glutinous rice intake. Wouldn't mind revisiting when venturing around the area; especially after shopping and settling in for some cozy starch bombs. That's what sushi is after all, am I right? Lol. Keep it local & prosper! Until next time. :)

description: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream – Montrose serves Montrose, Houston as a local event experience, with events at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: Loved this little sweet perk! This ice cream spot is bright and cheery, perfect on this sunny Saturday visit. I've been to V.L. before, and the establishment was just as nice and clean, well organized like last time. The lines were non existent, so Lou and I grabbed our ice cream and got to comfortably sit indoors inside the shoppe. The scooper was friendly and allowed us to try a few samples. Spoon samples were metal spoons that we got to throw into the used spoon section. Interesting. I love coffee so I just went for the coffee affogato flavor, as well as the dark chocolate brownie flavor. Out of the two, the affogato was creamier and a lot more lush. It was easier to eat and had a nice and light coffee flavor. The brownie ice cream was a bit on the drier side, but still had good, deep chocolatey flavor. I mixed the two a bit to get a better viscosity. Spoons are cute and well rounded, made of plastic. We also tried the Texas rodeo sundae and root beer soda, which Lou paid for. Flavors were great, sundae was dreamy and creamy. Crunchy with the praline pretzels and fluffy whipped cream. Overall we had a great time. It's sweet to be. This perk is taking place throughout the week and ends on the 19th of June. Thanks for a cozy opportunity to revisit the Montrose Collective plaza. Until next time!

name: PJ's Coffee
description: PJ's Coffee is a coffee and tea stop in Mobile, with a focus on coffee & tea. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: Crisp, refreshing and sweet! I'm liking this location on Airport Blvd, in West Mobile. It's tucked in the same plaza as Whole Foods Market and a few other shops. This location has a drive thru and a lovely interior inside. Seating is limited but it's ample enough for this part of town. I absolutely adored the clean and quiet environment. Staff was friendly and helpful as well. I decided upon a cafe au lait - but make it iced! Asked for some honey as well, and boy was it an awesome bevvie. The drink was frothy and refreshing. Just enough milk to cut through the sharp notes of coffee bean. I do like the flavors that PJs has to offer. Hoping they can open more locations in the South. I'll definitely be back to try out their beignets, muffins and a warm bevvie next time around. Happy this location opened up in the Pinebrook plaza, especially with far and few cafes in the area. Hope it stays for good. Cheerios! Until next time. :)

description: Located in Chinatown, Houston, It's Neat To Be : Month at ROYCE' Chocolate is a local event experience offering events. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.

This spot is awesome and has such an international vibe because of the ingredients they showcase within their chocolates. Pistachios and so many other variations within their chocolate! I love it and purchased the pistachio variation (more of that on their main business page). Royce originates from northern Japan... From an area known for its dairy products. I have always loved products originating from Hokkaido, such as their milk breads and cheese tarts + many other items. These chocolates are of no other exception... So milky and creamy with every bite you take.. especially their famous 'nama' chocolates which were provided as samples for this particular perk. My favorite being their matcha 'nama' chocolate sample. Soo good. Love anything with matcha! You could taste the quality of the fine tea leaves meshed with the creaminess of the cacao beans. Service was good, prompt and attentive. Just stayed for a bit as I was headed to an appointment somewhere else. Everything was appreciated though in regards to chocolate samples and answering all of my questions. Thank you Jando and Houston for this great little perk for the month of May. Cheers and SYOY.

name: Smashburger - Galleria
description: Smashburger - Galleria serves Galleria/Uptown, Houston as a local event experience, with events at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: What a wonderful foodtastic event! Thank you Houston and Jando for putting this together during the mid of April. Clear and sunny skies called for a milkshake paired with burgers and fries. Smashburger has been around for some time... scattered throughout Houston, but I had barely visited in the past. Simply because I don't eat burgers that often. But are they tasty? Most definitely. Whether stacked, smashed or simply a classic patty no cheese, you can't go wrong. I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich. Paired it with tator tots and a strawberry milkshake. No frills, just simple. Asked for avocado with my sandwich as well. Meal came out piping hot and fresh. The grilled chicken breast was on the smaller side, but still good. Buns were toasted and the tomato slices were fresh in the sandwich. The only thing that was missing was the avocado - they forgot to put it in the meal so I had to go and grab it. Avocado was a let down because it tasted dull and prepackaged, just as similar as the ones from Sam's club. Other than that, my meal was good. Fresh rosemary tossed into crispy and warm tator tots? Goood stuff! As well as the sweet and creamy strawberry milkshake paired with the meal. Very nostalgic of childhood. Met with other Yelpers as we chowed down on good grub. Twas warm and friendly company on that bright day. Will I revisit this particular smashburger location? Most definitely. It's central within most spots in the inner loop. Thank you Houston for a scrumptious food week. It is so appreciated. Until next time!

description: In Duluth, Hepzibah's Sweet Shoppe operates as a local business centered on candy stores, chocolatiers & shops. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: Service was just okay. Walked in yesterday and experienced cold and awkward service. The shoppe owner seemed a bit indifferent and crass as well. Totally ironic within a sweet candy shoppe. The candy itself was neat - a few local products and many chocolate truffles to choose from. Plenty of generic candies as well that you'll find at other spots. Although the candy itself was good, it was way overpriced. Just a few pieces of candy cost close to $20. The bottom line? Chocolate truffles were delicious. Decadent and full of rich chocolate flavor. The English toffee looked good as well. I may get that next time I revisit Duluth. Service needs a bit of a revamp though. It's a small little shoppe. You can't miss it if you're shopping and browsing within the area. Try it for yourself if you have a sweet tooth. Here's hoping you have a sweeter experience.

description: Windmill Market & Produce is a North Palm Springs business best described as a sweets and bakery destination, with an emphasis on grocery, fruits & veggies, ice cream & frozen yogurt. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: The fresh date shake here was marvelous.. thick in viscosity, creamy and out of this world. The aroma reminded me of brown sugar and the flavor was warm, even though it was a cold and creamy milkshake. They use fresh dates that are commonly grown near and around the palm springs area. We didn't get to venture too deep within Palm Springs, but this was the closest market to us when we were venturing out of Joshua Tree. Folks were friendly and efficient with their service. We opted for the vanilla ice cream date shake, which is the original flavor here. The dates just melt in your mouth and are totally otherworldly, along with the fresh packaged dates that you can purchase here. They make for a great gift as well, and there are plenty of different flavors - my favorite being the dates rolled in dessicated coconut. All in all, this is a pretty neat spot. I'd love to revisit and try their savory foods and other items as well. Geographically, it's super cool to be surrounded by windmills nearby, literally and figuratively. When around and passing through the Yucca Valley, you can count on Windmill Market & Produce for a great beverage and perhaps a snack or two while cruising through your road trip. :) Until next time!

name: Event: Chef's Table at Yi Peng Thai Dining
description: Event: Chef's Table at Yi Peng Thai Dining is a Memorial, Houston business best described as a local event experience, with an emphasis on events. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: Well. What can I say? All my favorite platinum (black) folk already wrote essays upon essays about our grandeur Thai inspired evening in City Centre. It was a cosy summer night as we noshed upon food that was as big & bold with flavor, as our conversations were. First of all; I adore Jando; his bold and spunky persona is exactly what Houston was missing all this time. Like a gust of fresh East Coast air just chillin and vibin' with us. Thank you for making me laugh and spilling all the deepest and darkest depths of right on our table. Nothing about this was surface level shit, the hammer and axe broke through the table (¡gracias a Dios!). I was highly amused; as much as I was with the food that kept magically appearing in front of us. I kept thinking we would eat typical Thai cuisine that night. But that was far from our reality.. we were gifted with artisanal small plated meals that were decadent yet rich in taste. My favorites were the short ribs and crispy chicken. Thai tea was quite sweet yet refreshing in between savory meals. Their fresh coconut water was great as well. A bit of coconut meat and lightly iced, it was perfect in this summer season. Chef Jett was enthusiastic, energetic and fun to speak with. His name is quite huge in this city and it was lovely to finally meet with him. His wife and the rest of the culinary team were friendly and informative as well. Thanks to the Thai cultural ministry in their initiative to feed a bunch of platinum folk and tickle our taste-buds & minds. Now I have a strong longing and impulse to visit Thailand and nosh on penang curry that's sprinkled with just the right amount of kaffir lime leaves (a fav of mine). Aside from my wanderlust daydream, I had a great evening catching up with old-school folk. With summer finally ending (I think) it was a great initiative catching up and learning about prospective events & growth of the community. Much has changed in the past decade... The nostalgia of days gone by.. but this I know for sure.. so much growth and change will usher in more fun & unique events to come.. cheers and syoy! PS - thanks for the lippy balm/mints + other cute wee little gifts. The remembrance of a fun night will linger longer than the taste of those mints. *Besos*

name: Pythagoras
description: Pythagoras is a Sugar Land business best described as a casual restaurant, with an emphasis on vegan, cocktail bars, pizza. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby. Current status: Closed.
review: Such a cozy little spot! I'm liking this conscious food philosophy on a quiet yet nonchalant corner of Sugar Creek plaza. I've always liked this little part of town and Pythagoras vegan cafe is a warm and bright welcome in the area. I met up with friends this evening and we all enjoyed our meals. Despite the menu being primarily of vegan food choices; there really is something for everyone here. The menu is chock full of pizza choices, soups, salads and Persian food items. We started with their loaded vegan nachos as an appetizer and it was quite filling and crisp. Plenty of veggies and the vegan cheese doused on top had a good flavor. Nachos were light and a great sharing item with friends. I'm not vegan but I enjoy eating fresh vegan and vegetarian foods as often as possible. I love the fresh breads here; such as their sesame bread that comes with their Persian style eggplant dip. Delish. As well as their pizzas; the crust is crispy and the toppings are generous. I'm typically not a fan of vegan cheese, but theirs is quite good. I recommend their grapefruit sparkling drink (non-alcoholic) or their juices. It's great to have a new vegan food joint in the area. The theme of the restaurant is unique and their service was warm and efficient. Our waiter was friendly, communicative and often checked up on us. Thanks dear Pythagoras for enlightening our minds on a random summer evening. It's just simple Pythagorean math; our bellies were full and our hearts felt warm. What more would you want?

name: Sunday Press | Garden Oaks
description: In Oak Forest/Garden Oaks, Houston, Sunday Press | Garden Oaks operates as a coffee and tea stop centered on coffee & tea, acai bowls, sandwiches. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: My gosh - the menu here is so colorful, fun and quite extensive. You will find something for everyone here! Rejoice. This colorful cafe in more ways than one is serving up colorful, sweet and intricate food items. Upon first glance - it's their sweets and treats that keep me coming back for more. Been awhile since I glanced at a marble pound cake, macadamia nut cookie, snickerdoodle and swirly croissants all tucked behind a lovely glass display. Sunday Press has these one of a kind swirl croissants which are hard to find within the city of Houston. This spot serves up these rare gems and on top of that? They're quite good. Great YUM and CRISP factor with the right amount of filling of your choice - my fav being the matcha swirl croissant. For drinks selections: they've got everything you need! From cafe lattes, tea lattes and many other beverages to choose from - ours being the london fog latte. Sweet. Depth. And just the right amount of bergamot essence kissing the milky foam of the cup. In regards to food, you'll find sandwiches, soups, salad among many other items. Its almost hard to decide - I was torn between pasta salad or breakfast taco. I went for the brekkie taco and glad I did. It was one taco yet it was filling, warm and with plenty of flavor. I liked how the taco wasn't spicy and that the tortilla was warm, stretchy and fresh. They added plenty of shredded veggies to my veggie breakfast taco. It was filling and made for the perfect meal earlier in the day. If I'm ever here later in the day, I'll definitely opt for some type of salad to go with my tea. This spot fills up quick! We got here earlier in the morning and witnessed seats disappearing fast. Thankfully they have plenty of seating of all types. Many folks connecting and chatting while others studying or working on their laptops. With decently warm service within a unique colorful environment - I can definitely see why this place slowly causes traffic jams and gets packed within the day. I envision myself revisiting again sometime soon and ordering a few different items on the menu. Will be back when in the area, which is once in awhile. Thank you Sunday Press for your treats and good vibes.

description: Waffle De Lys is a Gatlinburg business best described as a local business, with an emphasis on waffles, food stands. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: Not that good... The waffle was warm but dry in taste and texture.. because of this.. it got stuck on the paper boat container that it came in. I have had better Belgian style waffles throughout my travels and this certainly wasn't it. Flavorwise it wasn't bad and the aroma was buttery and lightly sweet, but overall it was just okay in execution. Chocolate sauce and fruit were added on top. Initially I wanted a plain butter waffle but decided to add toppings to it as well. In regard to pricing, it gets expensive with the adding and layering of toppings. They have a decent hot beverage menu so I opted for their hot chocolate. Not bad, but just okay, like the waffle. Gatlinburg is quite a touristy area so the service was appreciated. This is a unique choice of dessert for that part of town. It was appreciated among the cafes that had pancakes and coffee, but was just hoping for a better flavor. Something with more butter, flavor, and tenderness to the waffle. At least you can walk around town with this portable dessert while sightseeing in Gatlinburg. Try it for yourself.

name: Sweet To Be : CRAVE Cupcakes - West U
description: Sweet To Be : CRAVE Cupcakes - West U is a local event experience in West University, Houston, with a focus on events. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: This was a cosy n' cute sweet to be! I'm so glad I made it back from out of town to snag a cupcake, cake pop and hot coffee?! Sweeeet! Literally. This location of CRAVE has been around forever and yet it was my first time steppin' in! Thanks for the opportunity! I've been to their other location before, which has also been around for some time. Remember the absolute obsession trend of cupcake shoppes opening up in the 2010's?? Yeah some of us are that old. One of the reasons why I don't visit CRAVE that often is because their cupcakes are too sweet for me. I do appreciate their variety, as well as how they serve coffee all day? Didn't know that until this recent visit. They're basically a coffee cupcakery shoppe that serves up pretty much any kind of caffeine. I had their toasted cinnamon coffee with a coconut cream cupcake and cake pop. I'm not sure what flavor the cake pop was? But it was okay. Too sweet, just like their cupcakes. What I do appreciate, is how their baked goods are so tender. Another spot not far from here makes their cupcakes too dry, like a brick, IYKYK, Y'all can spot that review from another time. Back to CRAVE: Each bite was tender n' soft, aromatic (thanks coconut!) n' creamy. Coffee was hot, fresh, and paired well with the sweet treat. It was 6ish pm and that did not stop me from having a cup of coffee with whole milk. Service was great, can't complain and the folks in the back were all smiles. They happily waved goodbye as we left, no crumb left behind, and bebe was with me as well. Warm vibrations and the wafting aroma of va va vanilla and butter. You're in for a real treat. They also have frosted cookies here and other sweet stuff. I'll try to revisit again in the near future, especially with knowing they have various types of coffee. Thanks Hou for giving us all this sweet opportunity to nosh on cupcakes. It's my birthday month and this was totally appropriate as well. Lol. Cheers n' toasting to decadent cupcakes this summer. Until next time!

R&B has some tasty beverage choices and it was not my first time visiting this spot within the land of Sugar. Quality of beverages and customer service is spot on. Brandon and Julia were friendly and answered any of the questions I had in mind. I ordered a fresh milk beverage (strawberry matcha tea with tapioca). Asked for half sweet, but Brandon mentioned the matcha is quite strong and bitter. Bumped it to 70% sweetness and it was perfect! R&B tapioca is always chewy with the right texture and flavor. All in all, the matcha blended well with the bright flavors of strawberry. Will definitely reorder this next time! Their milk teas in general are great. Plenty of options for flavors, mixins and toppings. Thanks Houston for presenting this sweet opportunity for the month of. This was a great spot to visit on a warm Monday afternoon. Getting the week started with a tasty caffeinated fix! Until next time! SYOY. :)

description: Located in West University, Houston, Office Hours at TSAOCAA is a local event experience offering events. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: Juicy brewin' tea drinks and crunchy lil' nuggets? My type of hour right here! Exclusive convos with the homie Jando? Yes please! I love office hours and this one was a real treat. This spot is cute, light and airy. Plenty of seating @ Tsaocaa without it being too big or too small of a space. The vibes were immaculate. Just right. I'm lovin' their tea menu here. What a neat spot! Happy they opened up a location in the HOU. Tried two different beverages and both were refreshing. The first had nata jelly (made with coconut pulp and pineapple flavoring) & the second drink consisted of tapioca pearls. Both were chewy and tantalizing, but I must say, the pineapple with jasmine tea and nata jelly were totally delightful. The floral notes of jasmine were quite aromatic and sensual. Perfumy without being overwhelming. Probably the best I've had. Thanks for the complimentary tea(s) Jando! As well as the loot, cute little trinkets scattered round' the table. The pizza cutter will come in clutch as well as the travel accessory bag. Always appreciated. It was a tasty Tuesday tea day. Spent with good chatter, caffeine and fruity chews. We also had the youngest yelper join in on all the fun. The bebe was all giggles and smiles. What a delight. Until next time!

description: Milk+Sugar is a local event experience in West University, Houston, with a focus on events. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.

But this new location in specific is a lot larger, brighter and cleaner than their original location. I still like their OG shoppe.. but this one? Absolutely ideal with location (geographically) as well as their huge parking lot that they share with several other store fronts. I have always loved the flavors @ milk + sugar. They are dreamy as well as the namesake of each flavor. Heart of Glass? So cute. Still a favorite flavor for moi and @ this location, it tasted just the same. The kids slingin' the ice cream allowed us to sample a few. I was already familiar with most of their flavors so just opted for my favs. Sweet n' delectable, smooth ice cream. I was really hoping to try their pandan flavor for the month of, but alas, it wasn't available on a Saturday night. I've had pandan ice cream elsewhere, so I'm hoping to catch this one here next time around. Absolutely grateful for this perk. It was a generous sweet treat that included a waffle cone. Cold dessert on a humid night. Crunch. Munch. Yum. Thank you Jando and for this cozy treat. It was perf' in every way. Until next time!

name: Black Bear Diner Sugar Land
description: In Sugar Land, Black Bear Diner Sugar Land operates as a casual restaurant centered on breakfast & brunch, american, diners. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of all the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes.. and yes.. some of my favorite diners are in California (my HomeState). On with the food. This spot has been tucked away within the land of Sugar since 2019.. I've been visiting since then and have always enjoyed the grub at BBD. Albeit, their are some days when the foods perfectly on par, and then on some days when its just okay. Within my most recent visit... lines were out the door, frigid air was kickin' in and groups of folks were simmering within the cozy diner. Thankfully a group of us were seated promptly and found good seats closer to the entrance. Due to the fact they were busy.. it seemed the food was just okay this time. I ordered a beef patty melt with fries and coleslaw. Fries were blonde in color, cold, and such few. Patty melt was okay. Pancakes were warm and tender as they typically are. With such a huge crowd on the weekends, food can be subpar at times. Other than that, I have always appreciated BBD's expansive menu. Their hot chocolate is sweet, warm and creamy, and their desserts are quite nice as well. Savory hot items such as their omelets and other sandwiches are typically good. Dining experience and service? Great. BBD has a nostalgic, woodsy, Nor'Cal feel that will make any nature enthusiast appreciative of their whimsical theme of all things bears and forests. They even sell a few bear plushies, socks, and all cuddlesy stuff at the front (where you pay). Service has always been warm and appreciative. Servers almost always check up on you. Though, they ought to put table numbers or order numbers on the table. At least twice during the weekend rush they brought out wrong food orders to our table. All in all, this is a spot that many cherish. Perf for families, friends and groups of folk that wanna chat over coffee, pancakes and all the sweeter things in life. Until next time!

name: Foodie Adventure KoreatownHTX
description: Foodie Adventure KoreatownHTX serves Spring Branch, Houston as a local event experience, with unofficial events at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood. Current status: Event / Not Applicable.
review: What a wonderful event. Thank you Luis M Chen for organizing and putting this event together. All on your own, as usual, you made it happen and everything went seamlessly and integrated the event with the theme. All things Korean food and stopping at HMART as the last part of the adventure tour! I remember when Luis mentioned Shabu style food, I was already intrigued from the get- go. Because of it having a Korean flair I knew that I would enjoy the food, simply because of the sauces, spice and many different condiments (banchan) veggies and herbs. That is what I got here as I inhaled my vegetarian style shabu and my friends equally enjoyed their meal as well. They have seafood and meat options as well and everyone dug in and went back for more for this AYCE style concept. Service was attentive and everything was well taken care of; Luis often checked on us as well which was appreciated. What a great host! I got to learn a few techniques in regards to Shabu and hot soup dining. I like this style as it's not a communal pot that you all dig out of. You can adjust the temperature of your soup as well or just turn it off, all with a remote on the side of the table. A few of us ventured off to Hmart afterwards in search of more unique goodies. We purchased rambutan, fresh nectarine and a few shelf items. It was fun exploring the grocery store with Luis and Chris, always good company and even more fun on a very crowded Sunday. Thank you for giving us all goodie bags at your foodie adventure gathering. It was great catching up with a few old school yelpers while munching on hot soup. Good seeing Victoria, Tabatha and Genea as well. Thank y'all for your humor, silliness and good company. Cheers and SYOY until next time!

I can also have a friend join, as long as they take care of their own accomodations. weeks are quite flexible with the demands of my busy maman schedule. Cheers for visiting before nap time! I missed out on this perk that took place 1 year ago, when the kebab shop had recently opened. This place is great! Good food and overall good service. Everything was fresh to order and tantalizing to the tastebuds. French fries were hot n crispy as well, kebab was juicy and bread was fluffy. The saffron rice was full of saffron (in a good way) and the jalapeno cilantro sauce and garlicky yogurt sauce were on point. Bébé and I enjoyed. This made for a nice hangout in the middle of the week with fellow friends. Last bit of August in this heat made us cool down with some iced tea as well. Thank you Jay, for joining me on this local adventure. I'll definitely revisit this location in the near future. TKS is in a diverse plaza with a clothing boutique and whole foods. Can't go wrong with that. Thanks Alejandro (@ TKS) Thanks community and Jando! Appreciate y'all.

name: Dandelion Cafe - Bellaire
description: In Bellaire, Dandelion Cafe - Bellaire operates as a coffee and tea stop centered on coffee & tea, juice bars & smoothies, breakfast & brunch. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: I've been to Dandelion Cafe twice now and I definitely like the concept of this place. The outside and the inside of the cafe are nicely decorated and inviting. Its cute and cozy to have this little cafe tucked in Bellaire Blvd. I think its wise to say that we need more coffee houses in that part of town. I live out in Sugar Land.. but I enjoy venturing out and supporting local business. Service is warm and friendly. Nice place to hangout with friends and family. The coffee here is great. They use Greenway Coffee, which also happens to be a local Houston favorite. The beans are smooth and aromatic. I've tried both the pumpkin spice latte & gingerbread latte. Enjoyed them during this holiday season. The syrups are handmade and you can certainly taste it in the beverages. The coffee is definitely what I see myself coming back to. The food? Not so sure about that. I've tried the veggie delight sandwich on both occasions when visiting Dandelion. First time around, the sandwich was loaded with the good stuff: marinated eggplant, caramelized onions, red pepper spread, grilled asparagus, mushrooms, etc. Served with a small cup of watermelon. Its a tasty vegetarian sandwich.. and it came with a lighter tasting bread the first time around.. kind of like french bread. The second time upon visiting, the sandwich was much smaller in size and the bread was darker. Didn't pair well with the roasted veg. Served with a little cup of pickles. Well. I wasn't impressed. If the portion size is going to get smaller.. so should the price. The prices are steep for whats offered on the menu. I did enjoy the stuffed french toast, and the bagel dots stuffed with vegetable cream cheese. They also serve soup, salads, and dessert here. There is a variety of drinks for everyone and not just coffee. Think i'll just stick to a cafe latte and something sweet off the menu. Simple cafe vibes. I recommend checking out this place.

name: Greenwich Market
description: In Greenwich, London, Greenwich Market operates as a neighborhood market and specialty shop centered on public markets. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: Beautiful market studded with lively handmade art, global food, and enthusiastic vendors. Greenwich Market is truly a hole in the wall kind of market. Its nestled inside a passageway in between buildings and its very unassuming. I had a wonderful time visiting this market on the weekend. It just so happened to be a weekend and the market was bustling with all kinds of people. I went on a Saturday afternoon and ended up revisiting on Sunday as well. All of the local artists are incredibly friendly and charming. I tried many samples of local foods and ended up consuming a few snacks and hot coffee. I highly recommend the Jamaican ginger cake - it's fantastic! The young vendors behind the stand were very friendly and talkative. We chatted for a bit and I decided on the ginger cake after taking a sample. The market has a great selection of desserts, fresh fruit juice, coffee, vegan and non vegan items. You will find many food trucks parked in the open area of the market as well. There are many displays of local art that you can purchase. Inside the market, you will find many galleries showcasing paintings, pottery, and botanical art. This is the place to visit when purchasing or deciding on gifts for loved ones. There are a few coffee houses located right outside the market as well. Red Door, Peyton & Byrne, etc. I definitely recommend visiting any of these cafes while browsing throughout London on a chilly day. Visit this market - you'll be in for a treat in a multitude of ways.

description: Located in Greenwich, London, Peyton And Byrne is a coffee and tea stop offering bakeries, coffee & tea, patisserie/cake shop. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: Definitely worth visiting before or after checking out the Greenwich Market. I happened to stumble upon this place after strolling through the market. Glad to have found it. The lovely display of cakes and pastries looking throw the window was tempting enough. Lucky for me, I ended up eating a healthy, colorful and tasty lunch here. It was quite crowded inside on a Saturday afternoon. Ordered a grain and herb salad with a honey baked gooseberry and stilton cheese tart. The salad was crisp, fresh and brimming with fresh herbs. The tart was buttery, cheesy with a sweet mellow taste from the gooseberries. It was a lovely vegetarian meal that went well together. Had a pot of rose tea as well and asked for a small bit of honey. The rose tea was soothing and delightful. Paired quite well with the meal. Peyton and Bryne offer a great selection of sandwiches, salads, tarts, and pastries. Everything is made fresh and makes for a quick meal. They have some nice tasting coffee as well. Service was a bit rushed on such a busy day. There's a diverse selection of cafes in the area. Peyton and Bryne stood out like a classic cafe to try when in London. Definitely left satisfied. Nice neighborhood with many shops and galleries. It'd probably drop by again if visiting in the near future.

description: In Downtown, Austin, Voodoo Doughnut operates as a coffee and tea stop centered on donuts, custom cakes, coffee & tea. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: This doughnut shop tucked on east 6th street is open 24 hours 7 days of the week! When you have a hankering for doughnuts.. this place will always be there for you. That's definitely magical for a shop called Voodoo Doughnuts. I'm glad that we have one here in Texas.. the far and few locations are tucked out in the West Coast. So.. this place did live up to its hype. Came here at night and this place was happening. That's normally not the vibe at doughnut shops. My sister and I dived in and grabbed a handful of different doughnuts. We came, saw, conquered and ate.. almost all of them. I recommend the apple fritter, any of the cake donuts, and the voodoo looking donut, which had a chocolate glaze to it. They were all scrumptious, fresh and fluffy. None of the doughnuts were crazy sweet.. if anything.. they were addicting. The doughnuts were packed in their large iconic pink shaped box. Sat inside and enjoyed them. Quite a large crowd on a weekend night. The decor inside is funky, colorful and lively. Staff was friendly as well. If you're strolling through 6th street.. I definitely recommend dropping by. Grab some doughnuts and enjoy in good company. Parking for us wasn't a problem as we parked in the garage and wanted to have a nice walk. Trust me.. you'll need that walk after pecking on a few doughnuts. Until next time Voodoo.. you're spooky good.

name: Anonymous Café
description: Located in Sugar Land, Anonymous Café is a coffee and tea stop offering cafes. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: I've been coming to Anonymous Café since the summer and I must say.. they do not disappoint! I enjoy visiting this cozy Greek style coffee house. It's a bit small inside but that definitely adds to the overall charm of the place. Its appealing and quaint inside with just a few tables and chairs. There is even a sofa chair to cozy yourself up on. I have tried both Greek iced coffees and they are quite strong. I do not suggest these drinks if you are not into strong coffee. They are bitter and dark. I always ask for extra milk. Sometimes there's more ice than substance. So definitely make sure you get more coffee and less ice! Otherwise, its kind of a ripoff. Anyway, at least that's how I see it. There are lattes as well, which are quite nice. I absolutely enjoy the Greek desserts here. They are virtually difficult to find in Sugar Land and I suggest the honey & nut cookies, as well as the eckmeck. The eckmeck is a layered dessert consisting of shredded phillo, custard and cream. Topped with some toasted almonds and powdered sugar. It is heavenly! I enjoy the fragrant and syrupy desserts and they pair quite well with any coffee. I have not tried the pound cakes.. yet. But they look plump and tasty. They offer savory meals but I have not tried anything off the savory menu yet. The food served here looks fresh and homemade, so I definitely want to try it next time around. Besides, Greek food is know to be healthy! You just cant say no to a Mediterranean diet. :) Anyway, the folks running this place are quite friendly. They make you feel welcomed and at home. I highly suggest supporting this local business and I believe they deliver some of the best coffee in SL. Until next time!

review: Unique establishment serving up Armenian goodies which was a first for me. I love visiting international bakeries and was pleased with the items served inside the glass cases. There are so many items to choose from, including packaged goodies that you can take with you. I opted for the vanilla custard ponchik - which is deep fried bread with a sweet filling. Basically a Mediterranean doughnut. There are many flavours to choose from, in terms of the ponchik, but I liked the option that I settled for. I also ordered the sweet cheese roll. It took a few minutes for my order to be ready. They are made to order and served warm. I enjoyed the creamy custard filling and the crisp dough. The sweet cheese roll was nice and simple. Young women in the front were friendly and attentive. Many families were coming in and out of the bakery - i'm sure its quite popular in the area. Anyway, i'll definitely be back to try other items off the menu. My sweet tooth was satisfied and I left with a happy belly!

name: Flower Flour
description: Flower Flour is a Willow Glen, San Jose business best described as a sweets and bakery destination, with an emphasis on bakeries, custom cakes, patisserie/cake shop. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: Such a lovely little gem of a bakery tucked in a nice little neighborhood! I happened to be walking in the area and the shoppe simply caught my attention. The outside of the cafe is painted with a beautiful mural of cake and all things cute. Selling pretty flower's in a bakery? It's not anything new.. its so "European-ish!" I've always dreamed of opening a cafe with such a concept as my own. Seeing this concept in reality was lovely. Who wouldn't want to buy a bouquet of flowers to go along with a cake? It was a delight entering the cafe and noticing the pretty little cakes and pastries. The breakfast and lunch menu were intriguing, and I decided to settle for a savory crepe. To my surprise, it was amazingly delicious and one of the best crepes I ever had. The crepe was slightly sweet and salty, consisting of roasted vegetables and cheese. It was a flavorful vegetarian crepe that wasn't missing any meat. The meal itself was quite filling and my belly was delighted. I paired my meal along with a caffe latte, which in all honesty, wasn't the best that I've had. They also have morning buns, which had run out by afternoon. Haven't explored the pastries in depth but will try them next time around! I hope Flower Flour continues to do well.. they display a lovely presence in a quiet neighborhood. Go try them out for yourself!

name: Pho Ben - Sugar Land
description: Pho Ben - Sugar Land serves Sugar Land as a Vietnamese dining spot, with vietnamese, soup, noodles at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Always such tasty Vietnamese food! It's literally in my neighborhood and I find myself coming here a few times around. I should visit more often as its convenient, clean, and has simple and light food. I enjoy Vietnamese cuisine, as many of the foods are crisp, fresh and not greasy. Pho Ben has great prices and the portions of the food are quite large. They only use the freshest ingredients. Every time I come here, my belly feels happy and full, and I often have leftovers. This place is almost always packed, but you are guaranteed to find a table anyway. Tucked in the suburbs, you'll mostly see big groups of family's chowing down on some good grub. I have tried the banh mi here, rice noodle bowls, and fried rice with shrimp. Everything that I have ordered here has always been flavorful and colorful. The food is generously topped with fresh herbs and vegetables. I recommend this small restaurant if you're looking into something nice and different. In this hot and lengthy summer heat, I most definitely recommend the rice noodle bowls. They are crisp, light, and full of flavour. Yummo. Until next time!

name: Sambalatte
description: Sambalatte is a The Strip, Las Vegas business best described as a coffee and tea stop, with an emphasis on coffee & tea, desserts. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: Probably the best and most unique coffee house on the strip. Literally - the strip is cluttered with cookie cutter restaurants and chains. Sitting down and sipping on some exotic coffee here was pleasant and relaxing - I literally felt like I was no longer in Vegas.. Which is exactly what I needed to feel. I like the aesthetics, ambiance and feel of this place. Nice lights, colors, and overall interior design is lovely. I have a thing for rose flavored foods and drinks - so I truly enjoyed the rose petal latte. It is a coffee beverage that I literally cannot find anywhere else, unless I make something similar at home. It was foamy, warm, sweet and pleasantly scented. Come and try this unique latte at the Sambalatte. They have nice pastries as well. I opted for the banana bread - It was thick and dense, with good flavor. It wasnt too sweet. I would totally visit this cafe next time around, but I barely visit Vegas. Try this coffee house if you love lattes and anything coffee related. Staff isn't that warm and the prices are a bit steep.. but it's Vegas. Oh well. Its a nice little spot to relax and catch-up with others if you're in the area.

name: Shake Shack Las Vegas - NYNY Hotel
description: Shake Shack Las Vegas - NYNY Hotel is a sweets and bakery destination in The Strip, Las Vegas, with a focus on burgers, ice cream & frozen yogurt, fast food. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: Yum! I made sure to try out Shake Shack in LV, since I missed out in NYC (where its originally from). So the lines here are always incredibly long, but the process was pretty quick. Didn't have to wait for too long. Nice and open space with many windows and proper seating. Their were many young people here just chowin down on some fancy fast food grub. I opted for the mushroom burger (its a fried mushroom burger with cheese). Felt like eating vegetarian, as its the option I primarily try to choose when dining out. Ordered some fries and the chocolate concrete as well. The food was decent, mushroom burger was a bit on the small side. It was a bit difficult to eat as the mushroom became rubbery and chewing after getting fried. French fries were okay. The chocolate concrete with the chocolate sprinkles was probably the best thing I ate. It was creamy and luscious. Their were a few brownie bits sprinkled in, but definitely not enough. Overall, my experience at Shake Shack was okay, not too bad. I'll definitely try something new off the menu if and when I visit. Supposedly they'll be bringing a location to Houston, TX. Until then!

reviewPage.theExperience: The visit was mixed overall.

name: Dumpling And Noodle House
description: In The Strip, Las Vegas, Dumpling And Noodle House operates as a local business centered on chinese, noodles. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: This place is not bad.. Rather its a little hole in the wall spot to visit when in the Vegas Strip. I'm not too fond of fast-food, and Vegas seems to be cluttered with those sort of options. I enjoy piping hot Asian food, and that is what I found in this little Chinese restaurant. It seems a bit lonely and run down. But once you enter, you're greeted warmly by the servers. Their werent that many people inside, but it didnt really matter to me. I went ahead and ordered the crispy scallion pancakes, hot milk tea, and pad thai with tofu. The best item from my order was the scallion pancakes. They were crisp, hot and fresh. It's more of an appetizer item, but scallion pancakes have always been a favorite of mine so I was pleased by their appeal and flavor. I already knew that ordering pad thai at a Chinese restaurant was not the best idea, but luckily it wasnt too bad. The flavor was not authentic, but it still tasted fresh. The tofu was soft and crisp, and the noodles were tender. I would give it 3 stars. The Chinese style hot milk tea did not taste good at all! I would give that beverage a 1 star. I am a big fan of milk tea, but this drink did not deliver the taste that i was craving. They also have tapioca here, but im glad I did not order that. I'm not too sure if it would have been any good. Anyway, the menu is quite large. I was hoping their would be a vegetarian option for dumplings, but their wasnt. This place doesnt have the best food on the strip, but its not awful either. I would maybe try other items off the menu if I were to visit again. Nothing to write home about. Just hot food without all the junk.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: At Dumpling And Noodle House, the meal on this 2016.0 visit revolved around tea, milk tea, tapioca, and noodles. Texture and crispness did most of the talking, and the overall impression was mixed.
reviewPage.theExperience: Service felt friendly and attentive.

name: Waffle Bar @ Venitian
description: Waffle Bar @ Venitian serves The Strip, Las Vegas as a local business, with waffles at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Yum! Authentic Belgian liege waffles in the Vegas Strip. Would have never known to have found this gem of a place while visiting the city. This little outdoor food stall offers some great and authentic Belgian style waffles. I was in the mood for a simple waffle with no toppings or anything. Didn't want the extra sugar and the prices were quite steep as it is. The plain Belgian waffle was so delicious, buttery and crispy! The pearl sugar in each bite brought a caramelized taste. Smelled like a sweet and simple crepe. I had always wanted to try this type of waffle and I finally got to. If you're looking for a unique sweet treat, then I urge you to visit this little stall. It certainly aroused my attention after mostly observing cookie cutter restaurants and places to eat in the strip. Oh and it's a sweet treat that is quite big so it's easy to share with others.

description: The Guest House is a Los Feliz, Los Angeles business best described as a casual restaurant, with an emphasis on cocktail bars, new american, venues & event spaces. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: Just okay. A bit on the pricey side and reeks of hipster vibes. Do like the cozy home-style establishment and the furnishings. Coffee was good and tea is served in small mugs but you can totally get a refill on tea if needed. Cakes and pastries are nice and the coffee house is tucked in a cool neighborhood.

name: Couscous a Gogo
description: Located in Beverly Hills, Couscous a Gogo is a restaurant focused on regional South Asian and Middle Eastern flavors offering mediterranean, sandwiches, middle eastern. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: My sister and I enjoyed a delicious and memorable meal here as we ate outside on a cool weekday night. Both the concept and ambiance are totally unique. Anis (the owner) made us feel welcomed and comfortable. He made my sister and I feel like family, as we happily chatted with him about Mediterranean/North African cuisine. I totally dig that kind of food - from those warm and rich cultures full of hospitality. That is what we received here at Couscous a Gogo. I was craving a warm and hearty plate of couscous with meat, so I ordered the beef couscous plate. The stew was tender with succulent pieces of beef and hearty chunks of root vegetables. Served on a bed of steamed couscous. I asked for a bit of harissa (hot sauce) which totally complimented the meal, and you cant go wrong with harissa and couscous! My sister enjoyed her rosemary chicken sandwich. The grilled chicken was tender and full of flavor. Fries were my least favorite. They were lukewarm and thin - didn't remind me of pomme frites. Anyway, I often eat vegetarian, but the meat is exceptional and of good quality. Meatless items are also served up on the menu - if ya swing that way. They use fresh and local ingredients in the food and you can simply taste it in every bite. Yummy! Wish I could eat some couscous right about now. It is so comforting and I totally left with satisfaction and a warm happy belly. Please give this local establishment a chance. The whole staff is so welcoming and super kind. They are crafting up some light, healthy and innovative food that will tickle your tastebuds! I will definitely be back when visiting the area and will try something new. Until then. Au revoir!

name: Caffè Bene
description: Caffè Bene is a coffee and tea stop in Downtown, Houston, with a focus on desserts, coffee & tea, waffles. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: Tried this place out when they newly opened in Houston. I gotta say, I was so happy when they brought a location down to HTX! Having tried it in NYC a few times, I often wondered why we didn't have one ourselves. Well, Caffe Bene has finally arrived to Houston and its a great and unique choice compared to other standard coffee shops (especially Starbucks). Blech!Anyhow, I like their frozen and iced beverages the best. Especially since the weather has been quite hot here lately. They also have gelato, which I have tried and it was good. Many other desserts to choose from, such as honey toast bread, waffles, etc. Anyhow, its located within the Houston Pavilions, which is a nice yet quaint shopping center. All surrounded in the heart of downtown. Caffe Bene is a unique Korean style coffee shop. I definitely recommend you try this place out if you get a chance!

name: Thierry André Tellier Café
description: Thierry André Tellier Café is a sweets and bakery destination in Galleria/Uptown, Houston, with a focus on bakeries, desserts, french. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: "Aw, what a cute little patisserie!" Those were the words that came out of my mouth as I found this little gem, tucked in Uptown Park. It was also my first visit to the park. Small, pretty, with little shops here and there. I have only came in here on a few visits to pick up sweets. Almond croissant is the first word muttered out of my mouth, as I explain to the cashier on what to fill my bag with. Then comes scones, brownie, and cranberry bar. The almond croissant is generously loaded with almonds, and marzipan. It is huge, and can feed up to three people. Thats if you don`t mind sharing!;) The Swiss brownies have the perfect amount of semi sweet cocoa, and have a chewy moist taste. They are definitely the gourmet fix for brownies! Scones are heavy, and crumble in your mouth. Just the way they should be. It is dotted with crispy cinnamon sugar. Cranberry bars are refreshingly zesty! A nice blend of sweetness with just the right amount of tartness. The lemon gives it a clean taste. Oh yes... also petit fours! How can I forget to mention them. They are mini little cakes that are wrapped around a green coloured marzipan layer. The inside of the cake is layered with a soft filling of raspberry. Quite wonderful! I want to try out Thierry's for lunch one day. Not sure if its any good? I may give it a try, seeing how I have been pleased with their treats.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: At Thierry André Tellier Café, the draw was the experience itself: cake, brownie, and croissant. What made it memorable was texture and crispness, not just the activity on paper.
reviewPage.theExperience: The setting felt clean and comfortable.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: Yes. The overall experience was strong enough to revisit.

name: Fellini Caffè
description: Fellini Caffè is a West University, Houston business best described as a coffee and tea stop, with an emphasis on italian, coffee & tea. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: Brillante! Fellini Caffe offers various authentic Italian style pastries, beverages, and savoury items. I absolutely adore the layout of this cafe as well as the ambiance it portrays. I came here with my friend about a month ago - overdue review! The lady who I met was kind and showed me around. She gave me a detailed tour around the pastries which I was quite fond of. I was pleased to find out that the pastries are made by an Italian Chef. Given the aesthetic appeal of the desserts I could easily believe that. My friend and I ordered various pastries, savory items and the creme espresso. I enjoyed the creamy espresso, but it was too sweet for my liking. Other than that, I appreciate how there are several coffee items on the menu. Many of them are unique and sound exquisite since they are of an Italian profile. Same goes for the desserts, which I enjoyed every bit of. This cafe is truly a work of art and a gem that's located in Rice Village. I am looking forward to trying out more items the next time I come around.

reviewPage.theExperience: Service felt friendly and attentive.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: Yes. The visit gave Sara a reason to return and try more.

name: Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt
description: Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt is a sweets and bakery destination in Missouri City, with a focus on ice cream & frozen yogurt. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: I've been coming here for a couple of years now. The yogurt cafe is always clean and organized. There's never any sticky yogurt on the floor nor clinging to the pumps. I love the colorful interior and chairs as well. There is one complaint though - the lack of flavors. Having come here for a few years, the flavors start to get repetitive. It would be nice if they can change up their flavors from time to time. The bright side is that my favourite flavours such as coconut and lychee are always present. A better selection of fresh fruit would give this place some diversity as well. I stay away from putting candies in my yogurt as it gets too sweet. All in all, Frutti Tutti is in a convenient location. Nice way to drop by every once in awhile when a yogurt craving hits.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: A few of the house offerings set the pace for this visit to Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt. From there, the sweeter side of the visit helped decide whether the stop felt ordinary or worth remembering.
reviewPage.theExperience: The setting felt clean and comfortable.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: No. Based on this visit, Sara did not plan to return.

name: Caffe Vero
description: Located in Albany, Caffe Vero is a coffee and tea stop offering coffee & tea. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: It's too bad that this cute little coffee house closed down. I remember being here a year ago when I last visited Albany. Hoping that there will be a few other coffee gems such as Vero in Albany soon. Really enjoyed their pumpkin Nutella latte. It was the perfect beverage that hit the spot in such a cold little wintry town.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: Our pick at Caffe Vero was latte and coffee. The experience had a charming rhythm, with the coffee standing out most.
reviewPage.theExperience: The visit was mixed overall.

name: Les Givral's Sandwich & Cafe
description: Les Givral's Sandwich & Cafe is a Midtown, Houston business best described as a Vietnamese dining spot, with an emphasis on vietnamese, sandwiches, soup. Its location makes it relevant to people already spending time nearby.
review: I'd been wanting to come here for sometime.. and I finally made it happen! Les Givrals is tucked in a cute little corner in midtown. I have been to a few of the cafes right across this restaurant.. but all this time I mainly had my eye on this gem. The quiet cafes that are in the same plaza as Les Givrals are just okay. Meaning the food and the ambiance were not that great. Les Givrals was quite busy and bustling on a Friday afternoon. I had errands to run, so I made a to-go order of their shrimp fried rice. The decision was a great one. The fried rice was savory, garlicky and aromatic. Probably the best fried rice I've eaten in a long time. The shrimp was generous, steamy and plump. I loved how the dish was garnished with fresh cilantro as well. The order took some time, but I didn't mind the wait. I ordered soft shrimp rolls while my order was being made. The soft shrimp rolls were nice and healthy. Juicy pieces of shrimp and tofu were tightly tucked into the roll and came with a traditional hoisin dipping sauce. Vietnamese food is definitely a favorite. I love how each dish is fresh and has its own appeal. I'm looking forward to trying the banh mi next time i'm here.. as well as the cafe su da (Vietnamese coffee) for a nice pick-me-up. Good service and a clean cafe with many tasty and authentic food options. Will definitely be back soon!

reviewPage.whatWeTried: Our pick at Les Givral's Sandwich & Cafe was soft shrimp rolls and errands to run, so I made a to-go order of their shrimp fried rice. The experience had a laid-back and lively rhythm, with freshness standing out most.
reviewPage.theExperience: Service felt friendly and attentive. The setting felt clean and comfortable.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: Yes. The visit gave Sara a reason to return and try more.
reviewPage.whatWeOrdered: soft shrimp rolls; errands to run, so I made a to-go order of their shrimp fried rice

name: Tartine Bakery
description: Tartine Bakery serves Mission, San Francisco as a coffee and tea stop, with bakeries, cafes, desserts at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Great selection of desserts. But just okay. I ordered a seasonal berry frangipane tart. The bottom of the dessert was charred and over baked. The black bottom of the tart created a burnt and bitter taste in my mouth. Not so good. The brioche bread pudding had too much of an eggy taste and was not sweet enough. It was just okay. I did like the generous amount of berries on top. I think i'm more used to sweet and rich bread puddings since I live in the South. The only dessert that I did like was the tres leches cake. I loved the incorporation of the buttery crust against the smoothness of the milky cake. Delish. The cafe au lait was nice as well. I fancied the large bowls the cafe au lait was presented in. Yes, I am snobby when it comes to desserts. I have a degree in baking and pastry. Tartine was just okay in my experience but I would not mind coming back again and trying something new!

reviewPage.theExperience: The visit felt generally positive.
reviewPage.whoMightEnjoyIt: Coffee or tea drinkers and dessert lovers.

name: Hatam Restaurant
description: Hatam Restaurant serves Anaheim as a restaurant focused on regional South Asian and Middle Eastern flavors, with persian/iranian, halal, kebab at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Great food, great service and great location! The kebabs at Hatam are juicy and brimming with lots of flavour! Try the lubia polow. Its a seasoned rice dish with chunks of stewed beef, spices, and green beans. A nice change from plain steamed white rice. I love that Hatam's has a unique selection of rice and kebab dishes. There are many choices that suit anyone's flavour palate. The stews are a great choice as well. The folks that run this establishment are warm and friendly. I am glad to see their business doing well. Do yourself a favour and stop by this place! Your belly will thank you.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: This was a slow-down-and-try-it kind of stop at Hatam Restaurant, built around rice, kebab, and beef. The level of heat gave the visit most of its charm.
reviewPage.theExperience: Service felt friendly and attentive.

name: Tea Bar and Organics
description: Located in Sugar Land, Tea Bar and Organics is a coffee and tea stop offering bubble tea, asian fusion, tea rooms. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: So I believe this is the original location of Tea Bar & Organics. The cafe is larger and has far more seating options than the location in Sugar Land. I prefer this location since it's in the heart of Bellaire. There are so many little shops here and I love visiting after a nice outing in the area. I like the vibe and ambiance of this spot. Its always crowded, but you're sure to find a seat. There are many drink, dessert and food options on the menu. Whether its cold or hot outside, I tend to always chose a warm beverage off of the menu. My favorite drink is the hot honey milk tea. I suggest getting this tea with real whole milk and toning down the sugar to 2/3 sweet. The honey milk tea is warm, sweet and satisfying. One of the best that I have had. I love the aroma as well. The milk tea comes in these cute little mugs that are sure to satisfy. What I love most about Tea Bar & Organics is the diversity of the menu. The staff is nice as well and they are prompt with their service. There is something for everyone here.

reviewPage.theExperience: Service felt friendly and attentive. The space was busy during the visit.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: Yes. The overall experience was strong enough to revisit.

name: Copenhagen Bakery & Cafe
description: In Burlingame, Copenhagen Bakery & Cafe operates as a sweets and bakery destination centered on bakeries, desserts, custom cakes. The business adds a distinct stop to the area's broader dining, shopping, and service landscape.
review: My favourite bakery when visiting California! I love the unique array of Scandinavian style desserts at Copenhagen Bakery. My favorites are the princess cake, cinnamon rolls and cheesecake. I love how each dessert is uniquely its own. Copenhagen has a great selection of breakfast and lunch items as well. They have a nice array of tea, coffee, smoothies and hot chocolate. The baked loaves of bread look tempting here as well. There is something for everyone here. Just about everything is lovely about this bakery and it is totally worth the stop when visiting the city.

reviewPage.whatWeTried: At Copenhagen Bakery & Cafe, we kept things focused on coffee, tea, hot chocolate, and cake. The stop felt enthusiastic, with the sweeter side of the visit doing the most to define it.
reviewPage.theExperience: The visit felt generally positive.
reviewPage.wouldWeGoAgain: Yes. The overall experience was strong enough to revisit.

name: Epicure Café
description: Epicure Café serves River Oaks, Houston as a coffee and tea stop, with bakeries, cafes at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Epicure is a quaint little gem in the River Oaks neighborhood. I find myself coming here often these days. Upon entering you'll notice paintings all around the cafe. These are beautiful paintings done by local artists. I believe they are for sale since there is a price tag on each painting. The artwork really pops out the environment here. The display of colorful desserts are eye catching as well. What im most tempted to get here are the cakes. So far I've tried both of the chocolate cakes, pistachio cake, and the apple pie. All of the desserts have their own unique taste. What I like most about the desserts here is that they are not overly sweet. The cafe au lait and the caffe latte are nice to pair with the desserts. I have tried both coffees and they are nice and strong. As far as the tea goes, I definitely recommend the lemongrass tea. It has a refreshing taste. I wouldn't recommend the hot chocolate though. It was pretty mediocre and tasted like Swiss Miss. The prices are a bit steep here. One slice of cake and a hot chocolate cost $8.92. I cant say much about the savory food, but there are a variety of items on the menu. Think of sandwiches, soups and omelettes. The food sounds good, but i'm always tempted by the sweets. Overall, Epicure Bakery is a charming little place to visit if you're in the area.

name: Coco Crepes, Waffles & Coffee - Rice Village
description: Located in West University, Houston, Coco Crepes, Waffles & Coffee - Rice Village is a coffee and tea stop offering creperies, coffee & tea, breakfast & brunch. This profile gives visitors a quick sense of what the business is and how it fits into the surrounding area.
review: This location of Coco's Crepes is tucked in a quiet little corner of Rice Village. Having been to the original Coco's in Midtown many of times, the new location in the village was a nice change of scenery. Upon entering, I noticed how clean it was inside and preferred the layout and space of the new cafe. My family and I decided to share a creme brulee crepe and ordered our own coffee beverages. The creme brulee crepe was a flavour that I had never tried before. Let me tell you this.. It was delicious! The crepe was large, fluffy and chewy. It was big enough for my family and I to share. The creme brulee crepe was filled with a decadent smooth pastry creme and sliced strawberries. The outside of the crepe was bruleed, which created a crispy texture, and was drizzled with chocolate sauce. The presentation was beautiful and we were all satisfied. Unfortunately, our coffee beverages that we ordered (cafe au lait & latte) never arrived to our table. I went up to the cashier/barista and reminded her of our order. In which case she looked confused because she had completely forgotten about our coffee! I was surprised that she had forgotten about our drinks, in regards to our small and simple order. She quickly made our drinks and brought it to our table. The girl was friendly yet seemed quite out of it. Maybe it had been a long day for her? Anyhow, my family and I still enjoyed our experience here. This location serves up waffles and a few other items as well. I may try a sweet waffle next time around. Coco's is always a nice little spot to visit for some good desserts and to bring family, friends, or out of town guests.

name: Saigon Pho and Grill Vietnamese Noodle House
description: Saigon Pho and Grill Vietnamese Noodle House is a Vietnamese dining spot in Sugar Land, with a focus on vietnamese, soup, sandwiches. It is part of the local mix of places to eat, shop, or spend time in the area.
review: Pretty decent tasting Vietnamese food in a clean and spacious environment. I like the classical music playing inside as I enjoy a healthy and colorful meal here. I've been to Saigon Pho & Grill twice so far.. and I have to say that its good. But my favourite in Sugar Land will always be Pho Ben. When I first came here.. I ordered soft tofu rolls and a tofu banh mi. Unfortunately, the tofu was missing inside of the soft roll. All I got was lettuce and noodles inside my roll. Where was the tofu? It was the main ingredient which was missing. Well... the world may never know. Haha! As far as the banh mi goes.. it was delicious and satisfying. The tofu inside the sandwich was crispy.. as was the bread. The vegetables inside were fresh and crunchy. I no longer have to make the drive to China Town when craving a good banh mi sandwich. Second time around I came here.. I was craving a big bowl of vermicelli noodles with crispy tofu and vegetables. Well.. that is exactly what I got here. It was delicious and healthy. Although I would have liked fresh herbs on top of the vermicelli bowl. Adding fresh herbs always brings out the flavor of an item. It's one of my favorite dishes as its light and the noodles are boiled and not fried. I also ordered the shrimp soft rolls. They were generously filled with plump and juicy shrimp. The peanut sauce always goes nice with this tasty item. Even though I was hungry and ate a lot for my standards.. I had plenty of leftovers to take home. The cafe su da (Vietnamese iced coffee) is always a crisp and caffeinated drink when in the mood for a buzz. I may be back for the tofu sandwich and to try out other items from the menu (vegetarian pho & such).

name: Paciugo Gelato & Caffè-Houston
description: Paciugo Gelato & Caffè-Houston serves West University, Houston as a coffee and tea stop, with ice cream & frozen yogurt, coffee & tea, gelato at the center of its offering. It is one of the local options people may come across while exploring the neighborhood.
review: Paciugo has a large selection of gelato and coffee beverages. At the time I visited, they had many holiday beverages. But.. The gelato here is strikingly sweet.. I had a difficult time in finishing the small cup of gelato I ordered. The flavour was there, but the sweetness was just too much for me and my family. I used to frequent Paciugo many years back when they were in Sugar Land. I feel as if the flavour was better at that location. Too bad they closed down. But on the bright side, their are a few other places in Houston that make a light tasting gelato without dumping in too much sugar to please the American palate. If this is your type of place.. then go ahead and indulge. The caffe was quite busy when I visited at night and the plaza is a popular spot among families and young people. The servers were friendly and I appreciated their service but I wont be frequenting anytime soon.
